The promised answer creates a second complaint

Habakkuk’s first complaint is about wrong inside Judah (verses 2–4). God’s answer is the coming of Babylon (verses 5–11). That answer creates a second complaint. Verse 13 argues from God’s own character. A pure God is using a nation worse than the one it punishes. Verses 15–17 picture people as fish and the empire worshiping its net. The book records a prophet arguing with God.
The victimized peoples gain a voice against their captor

Verse 6 says the conquered peoples will speak these woes. They receive a voice against their captor. Verses 9–11 concern a house built with unjust gain. The builder hoped to set his nest out of harm’s reach. Verse 11 says the stones and beams themselves will accuse him. No human witness is needed. Verse 4 tells the righteous how to live while they wait.
The song chooses joy without claiming that food has returned

Verse 17 lists six losses. Figs, grapes, olives, grain, sheep, and cattle all fail. That is the whole food supply of a farming land. Verse 18 begins with “yet.” Nothing in the list is said to return. His joy is placed in God, apart from the harvest. Verse 16 shows that his body still trembles as he says it.
